section_summary: This section details the post-World War II administration, repair, and policy disposition of Japanese international submarine cables and related telecommunication facilities between September 1945 and December 1949. It covers Allied and U.S. inter-agency discussions—involving the State Department, War Department, Navy Department, and SCAP—regarding the lifting of wartime restrictions, commercial repair requests by the Commercial Pacific Cable Company, and the operation of the cable ship Tsurishima Maru. In addition, it documents U.S. trusteeship considerations for Japanese cables, the resumption of cable operations by Denmark's Great Northern Telegraph Company at Nagasaki, and Japanese Foreign Office proposals and State Department planning for cable disposition in the prospective Japanese peace treaty.

subfiles.about: Transmitting a service message received from RCA's New York office reporting the removal of Japanese telecommunication restrictions.

subfiles.to: Rear Admiral Joseph R. Redman (Director of Naval Communications, Navy Department)

subfiles.about: Bringing earlier Navy Department recommendations regarding Japanese-owned cable facilities to the attention of George P. Baker.
subfiles.from: Rear Admiral Joseph R. Redman (Chief of Naval Communications, Navy Department)

subfiles.title: Joint Letter Recommending U.S. Acquisition and Seizure of Japanese Submarine Cables
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf (Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether the Japanese cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru may be chartered to repair Far Eastern cables for commercial cable companies.
subfiles.from: Frank Flynn (Vice President, Commercial Pacific Cable Company)
subfiles.summary: Commercial Pacific Cable Company inquires whether Japanese cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru can repair Far Eastern commercial cables and requests per diem rates.
subfiles.title: Letter Inquiring on Availability of Japanese Cable Ship Tsurdishimi Maru
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf (Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Asking the War Department to ascertain from SCAP whether Japanese cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru is available to repair commercial cables.
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf (Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Requests the War Department query SCAP on the availability and per diem charge of cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru for commercial repairs.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Requesting SCAP Query Regarding Cable Ship Tsurdishimi Maru
subfiles.to: Operations Division, War Department General Staff

subfiles.about: Informing Commercial Pacific Cable Company that their inquiry concerning the cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru has been referred to SCAP in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf (Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Informs Commercial Pacific Cable Company that their request regarding the Japanese cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru was referred to SCAP in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Letter to Frank Flynn Concerning Referral of Cable Ship Inquiry to Tokyo
subfiles.to: Frank Flynn (Vice President, Commercial Pacific Cable Company)

subfiles.about: Routing SCAP correspondence regarding the control of Japanese international submarine cables to the Operations Division.
subfiles.from: Lieutenant Colonel Matthew C. Smith (Assistant Secretary, General Staff, War Department)
subfiles.summary: War Department routing slip transmitting SCAP correspondence regarding the control of Japanese submarine cables to the Operations Division for information.
subfiles.title: War Department Disposition Slip Routing SCAP Correspondence on Japanese Cables

subfiles.about: Concurring in principle with U.S. trusteeship over Japanese international cables and presenting detailed surveys of Pacific cable networks and repair facilities.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP)
subfiles.summary: GHQ SCAP concurs in principle with the United States assuming trusteeship on behalf of the United Nations over Japanese-owned international submarine cables and landing rights, while recommending no U.S. responsibility for rehabilitating cables not required by occupation forces. The document includes six detailed annexes listing the length, condition, ownership, and operating history of cables connecting Japan with Korea, the Bonin and Ryukyu Islands, China, Formosa, and Sakhalin. It also reports that the 1,200-ton cable repair ship Tsurishima Maru and domestic cable manufacturing facilities are sufficient to restore operations.
subfiles.title: Letter on Control of International Submarine Cables Owned and Controlled by the Japanese Government
subfiles.to: Chief of Staff, United States Army

subfiles.about: Transmitting SCAP's correspondence on Japanese international submarine cables and expressing War Department concurrence.
subfiles.from: Colonel R. L. Vittrup (General Staff Corps, War Department)
subfiles.summary: War Department memorandum forwarding SCAP's recommendations regarding U.S. trusteeship of Japanese international submarine cables to the State Department with War Department concurrence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Transmitting SCAP Recommendations on Japanese Submarine Cables

subfiles.about: Advising that SCAP reported cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru is fully engaged in occupation requirements and unavailable for commercial repair work.
subfiles.from: Colonel R. L. Vittrup (General Staff Corps, War Department)
subfiles.summary: War Department memo advising that SCAP reported cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru is required for occupational needs and cannot assist commercial companies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Unavailability of Japanese Cable Ship Tsurdishimi Maru

subfiles.about: Notifying Commercial Pacific Cable Company that SCAP cannot release the cable ship Tsurdishimi Maru for commercial cable repairs.
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf (Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Informs Commercial Pacific Cable Company that SCAP cannot spare the cable repair ship Tsurdishimi Maru from occupational duties for commercial repairs.
subfiles.title: Letter Advising Commercial Pacific Cable Company of Cable Ship Unavailability
subfiles.to: Frank Flynn (Vice President, Commercial Pacific Cable Company)

subfiles.about: Evaluating Commercial Pacific Cable Company's proposals for Pacific cable restoration, government subsidies, and future Japanese connections.
subfiles.from: H. B. Otterman (Telecommunications Division, Department of State)
subfiles.summary: Analyzes Commercial Pacific Cable Company's proposal for Pacific cable service, supporting equal competition with radio and priority assistance while advising against government subsidies and premature commitments regarding Chichi Jima ownership.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Commenting on Commercial Pacific Cable Company Proposal
subfiles.to: Mr. Cansler (Telecommunications Division, Department of State)

subfiles.about: Transmitting copies of the Japanese Foreign Office pamphlet "The Problems of Submarine Cables" for the State Department.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan (M. Weatherby)
subfiles.summary: Foreign Service despatch transmitting five copies of the Japanese Foreign Office's November 1948 pamphlet on submarine cables to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 224: Transmittal of Japanese Pamphlet on Submarine Cables

subfiles.about: Reviewing the history, wartime construction, and postwar condition of Japanese submarine cables, and presenting Japanese views on their disposition.
subfiles.summary: Published study by the Japanese Foreign Office reviewing the prewar development, wartime construction, and postwar condition of Japan's submarine cable networks. It details historical relations with the Great Northern Telegraph Company and the Commercial Pacific Cable Company, wartime naval cable laying, atomic bomb damage to Nagasaki facilities, and the 1948 agreement reopening the Nagasaki-Vladivostok circuit. The report appeals for Japan to retain ownership of international cables outside foreign territory, preserve Japanese syllabary telegraphy to Korea and the Ryukyus, and bar claims regarding restored Great Northern facilities at Nagasaki.
subfiles.title: The Problems of Submarine Cables
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Requesting coordinated armed services recommendations on the disposition of Japanese submarine cables for the draft Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.from: James E. Webb (Under Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Under Secretary of State Webb requests Secretary of Defense Johnson provide coordinated military recommendations regarding the disposition of Japanese-owned submarine cables for the forthcoming Japanese peace treaty, accompanied by clearance drafts.
subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of Defense Louis A. Johnson Regarding Japanese Submarine Cables in the Peace Treaty
